title: Density and distribution

blocks.heading: Density and distribution
blocks.text: Population density measures people per unit area; distribution describes where people live and how they are spread. A mean density can conceal concentrations. Density equals population divided by area, using comparable dates and boundaries.
context_tags: original teaching; fictional examples where stated

blocks.heading: Population density
blocks.text: Population density is the number of people per unit area, commonly people per square kilometre. A fictional 12,000 residents over 300 km² gives 12,000 ÷ 300 = 40 people per km²; it does not mean each square kilometre contains 40 people.
context_tags: original teaching; fictional examples where stated

blocks.heading: Population distribution
blocks.text: Population distribution is the spatial pattern showing where people live and how they are spread across an area. Describe clusters, sparse areas and relationships to locations using map evidence. A number per square kilometre does not describe the full spatial pattern.
context_tags: original teaching; fictional examples where stated

blocks.heading: Apply the measure
blocks.text: Calculate density for a fictional area with 12,000 people and 300 km². Show working. 12,000 ÷ 300 = 40 people per km².
context_tags: original teaching; fictional examples where stated

blocks.heading: Connect the ideas
blocks.text: Connect population evidence to Health (7.2), Education (7.3) and Urbanisation (4.2). Check dates, boundaries, denominators and units before explaining what a pattern supports.
context_tags: original teaching; fictional examples where stated
